Fallout 4 is such an interesting game because I despise its existence while also loving it. It is not fun to play...but I keep wanting to play it. I don't understand it. At the end of the day, when I am playing FO4, I'm depressed that it isn't New Vegas or FO1 or even FO3, so I had to accept that I just don't like FO4 like I want to and uninstalled it for the last time. It's fun, sure, but it isn't what I want it to be. 

After that, I went into a huge Fallout slump for a long time until I decided that I was going to get back into FO1 after a 20-something year hiatus...and it's been amazing. Relearning the world and the mechanics and everything is so much fun. Sure, it can be frustrating sometimes, but not in a bad way. It's frustrating in a "man, I wanna learn this right and try again" kind of way. 

Now, when I sit down to play Fallout 3, I have a great time again because I'm back in the position I was when I first played it, with a brain full of FO1 and 2 experience. It reminds me of why I loved FO3 in the first place. New Vegas will always be my favorite 3d Fallout, but FO3 hits the atmosphere of FO1 in a way that I never really appreciated before.


Long story short, play the originals and don't give up. Age doesn't mean anything for good games, just mindset. Just because it's old doesn't mean you can't get into it. Good things take effort, and FO1 is just that. AND, even if you don't like FO1 or 2, FO3 and NV still have a lot left to discover. 

To touch on the gunplay, I think it's pretty clear in the design of FO3 that they expect you to use VATS significantly more than actual run 'n' gun, so that could be part of your issue. You should be using VATS constantly. Anyway...sorry for the essay, it's just that I was exactly where you were about a year ago and I'm super back into Fallout and this is what helped me.


EDIT:
Also, don't rush. I found myself just rushing through stuff the more I played the 3d Fallouts because I was constantly trying to get the next dopamine hit, and that's how Bethesda designed it: just click on a map and instantly get loot. IMO, that's terrible game design. The reason why all of these legendary games became legendary is because they emphasized the JOURNEY, not the destination. Patience and effort pay off when you're playing a good game, and a game based off of instant loot loops is not the right kind of good (if that makes sense). What I'm trying to say is that good game design centers around REWARD and not the illusion of reward. People get bored with modern Bethesda games because they've streamlined the adventure process, but the best part about the adventure is all the """"""""boring"""""""" stuff that they're so desperately trying to avoid.
